messages:
Maya: Customer reports intermittent 401 during streaming (SSE) to /v1/streams. Provided request-id: req_20260317_9f3b. Says it works for a few minutes then 401s mid-stream. Need a minimal curl repro + what headers to capture.

Liam: taking this. quick Q: is customer going through a corporate proxy? any signed cookies in play?

Maya: customer said 'yes' to proxy and also rotating tokens (short TTL). No signed cookie mentioned. Logged: "auth_expired mid-stream" in service logs.

Nina: fyi, oncall-bot created INC-2026-331. attaching logs will help.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-331 created for streaming-401 spikes. Priority: P2.

Liam: ok plan: 1) get a curl that reproduces handshake+auth sequence 2) collect full curl trace (headers + body) 3) capture server-side request-id and timestamp pairs.

Maya: sending suggested curl. Ask customer to replace creds with REDACTED_TOKEN and sanitize domain.

Maya: ```bash
# keep connection open, show verbose headers, follow redirects
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_20260317_9f3b" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-small&session=abc123" \
  --trace-ascii curl_trace.txt
```

Liam: two extras to try if proxy is involved: `--http1.1` and `--no-keepalive` to force new TCP/TLS per request. Example: add `--http1.1 --no-keepalive`

Nina: capture the full verbose output: `curl --trace-ascii -` will stream curl trace to stdout. Ask them to include the trace file and the client-side timestamp when the 401 happened.

Maya: also ask for: 
- exact request-id header seen by server (X-Request-ID or x-amzn-trace-id)
- Authorization header value pattern (bearer vs signed cookie)
- proxy host + whether NTLM/kerberos used
- whether token rotation happens client-side or via refresh endpoint

Liam: server-side checklist for us to correlate: 
- request-id, server timestamps, auth-middleware logs around token check, TLS session reuse logs, upstream-proxy logs.

Maya: sample minimal reproduction notes to send customer: 
1) Run the curl above as-is, record curl_trace.txt.
2) If streaming drops mid-run, capture the last 3 lines of trace and note wall-clock timestamp.
3) If 401 is returned, copy the full response headers (curl -v shows them).
4) Try forcing a fresh connection: add `--no-keepalive` and see if token expiry race still occurs.

Liam: if they can't reproduce reliably, ask them to script a 60s keepalive loop and log every 5s: 
```bash
for i in {1..12}; do 
  date --iso-8601=seconds; \
  curl -sS -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
    "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?session=abc123" | head -n1; \
  sleep 5; 
done
```

Nina: request they run the trace and also collect a packet capture (pcap) for 30s if comfortable: `sudo tcpdump -w stream_repro.pcap host api.redwood.example and port 443` — this helps check TLS session reuse / renegotiation.

Maya: security notes to include to the customer: redact tokens before uploading. If they need help uploading, we can provide a temporary S3 upload link (support will generate).

Liam: for our side, we'll look for: token validation failures tied to refresh windows, proxy returning auth failures, or a load-balancer routing to an instance with stale keys.

Maya: sending to customer now. tagging @Nina for S3 link if they want to upload traces. :thumbsup:

Nina: I can generate a pre-signed upload. tell them to name files: req_20260317_9f3b_curl_trace.txt and req_20260317_9f3b_pcap.pcap

Maya: follow-up: customer returned curl_trace.txt and says 401 appears ~62s after initial connect. Attached snippet: 
```
== Info: Connected to api.redwood.example (1.2.3.4) port 443
> GET /v1/streams?session=abc123 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< X-Request-ID: req_20260317_9f3b
... (streaming) ...
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< Content-Type: application/json
< X-Request-ID: req_20260317_9f3b
{"error":"token_expired"}
```

Liam: 62s is suspiciously like a short TTL or proxy health-timeout. I'm going to check auth logs for token TTLs and the refresh flow.

Nina: pcap shows TLS session resumed on the second connection? I'll upload to the incident.

Maya: next steps for support ticket: 
- correlate server auth log for req_20260317_9f3b at t+62s
- check token issue time and expiry window
- ask customer if client performs token refresh mid-stream or prefetches new token and re-uses connection

Liam: hypothesis: client rotates token but keeps the same TCP/TLS connection; our auth layer validates token at request start and on some downstream checks mid-stream (e.g., metadata refresh), causing mismatch. If true, forcing new connection after token rotation fixes it.

Maya: will propose workaround while we investigate: either bump token TTL on their side, or make client re-open connection after refresh. Also we'll add a server check to not re-check token mid-stream for existing connections (engineering will evaluate regression risk).

oncall-bot: INC-2026-331 updated: investigator=Liam, evidence uploaded by Maya.

Maya: thanks team, closing loop with customer in thread. We asked them to try `--no-keepalive` and report back.

Liam: noted. I'll follow up with a runtime ticket if we find server-side cause.

Maya: thread done for now.
